rules.title: When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
rules.text: 2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).

rules.title: Power
A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting.
rules.text: 3.17.1. A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend’s power is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear and any curren…
rules.text: 3.17.2. A Unit or Legend’s power is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear and any current effect modifiers.

rules.title: A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.
rules.text: 3.17.3. A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.

rules.title: Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.
rules.text: 3.17.3.1. Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.

rules.title: A Gear’s power is equal to the power printed on the card.
rules.text: 3.17.3.2. A Gear’s power is equal to the power printed on the card.

rules.title: A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.
rules.text: 3.17.3.3. A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.

rules.title: “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.
rules.text: 3.17.4. “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.

rules.title: Textbox
rules.text: 3.18. ### Textbox

rules.title: A card’s textbox contains its card text.
rules.text: 3.18.1. A card’s textbox contains its card text.

rules.title: A card may have multiple textboxes.
rules.text: 3.18.1.1. A card may have multiple textboxes.

rules.title: “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2. “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.

rules.title: “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.1. “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.

rules.title: Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.1.1. Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts. See TERMS.

rules.title: “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2. “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.

rules.title: Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2.1. Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.

rules.title: Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2.2. Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.

rules.title: “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.3. “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.

rules.title: Flavor text is always italicized.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.3.1. Flavor text is always italicized.

rules.title: Card text addresses the player who played the card.
rules.text: 3.18.2. Card text addresses the player who played the card. When an effect says “you,” it’s referring to the player controlling the card.

rules.title: While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox.
rules.text: 3.18.3. While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox. See CARD TYPES > Gears.

rules.title: A card can be multiple types simultaneously.
rules.text: 4.2. A card can be multiple types simultaneously.

rules.title: Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.
rules.text: 4.2.1. Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.

rules.title: A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area.
rules.text: 4.4. A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area. All other areas (trash, hand, deck, etc.) are invalid areas.

rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.
rules.text: 4.4.1. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.

rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending.
rules.text: 4.4.2. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending. Remove the Legend from the game before you resolve them. See GAME AREAS > Removed from Game.

rules.title: To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
rules.text: 4.10. To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend. See Equip.

rules.title: By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
rules.text: 4.10.1. By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

rules.title: You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.
rules.text: 4.10.2. You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.

rules.title: There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.
rules.text: 4.10.3. There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.

rules.title: Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”
rules.text: 4.11. Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”

rules.title: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear.
rules.text: 4.11.1. The top textbox contains effects for the Gear. These effects are relevant when you play the Gear, and generally not relevant after a Gear is equipped.

rules.title: Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equip…
rules.text:
4.11.2. Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

rules.title: The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to.
rules.text: 4.11.3. The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to. Read the bottom textbox as if it's printed on that Unit or Legend.

rules.title: Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the G…
rules.text: 4.11.3.1. Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the Gear itself.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.
rules.text: 4.11.3.2. A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

rules.title: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.
rules.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

rules.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
rules.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

rules.title: If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new a…
rules.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

rules.title: When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order.
rules.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

rules.title: A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”
rules.text: 5.3. A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”

rules.title: If a game area is public, these rules apply.
rules.text: 5.3.1. If a game area is public, these rules apply.

rules.title: Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players.
rules.text: 5.3.1.1. Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players. You can look at information on all face-up cards at any time.

rules.title: Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known.
rules.text: 5.3.1.2. Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

rules.title: If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.
rules.text: 5.3.2. If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.

rules.title: Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known.
rules.text: 5.3.2.1. Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

rules.title: If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.
rules.text: 5.3.2.2. If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to…
rules.text: 5.3.2.3. If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to another area.

rules.title: When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fai…
rules.text: 5.3.2.4. When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fail to find a valid target. See Search.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may cho…
rules.text: 5.3.2.4.1. If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may choose to fail to find a target.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choo…
rules.text: 5.3.2.5. If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choose a legal target. You are not required to reveal it.

rules.title: If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not cho…
rules.text: 5.3.2.6. If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not chosen, return those cards to their original area in their original order and state.

rules.title: Legends Area
rules.text: 5.7. ### Legends Area

rules.title: Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.
rules.text: 5.7.1. Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.

rules.title: You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.
rules.text: 5.7.2. You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.

rules.title: While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.
rules.text: 5.7.2.1. While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.

rules.title: If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.
rules.text: 5.7.2.2. If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.

rules.title: “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.
rules.text: 5.7.3. “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.

rules.title: The Legends area is a public area.
rules.text: 5.7.4. The Legends area is a public area. Players can count the number of cards any player has in this area and read them at any time.

rules.title: The face-down Legends in this area are hidden.
rules.text: 5.7.4.1. The face-down Legends in this area are hidden. You cannot look at them unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival…
rules.text: 5.7.4.2. If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival without revealing them. This can be with a token marker, or by physically separating known Legends from unknown Legends.

rules.title: If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unles…
rules.text: 5.7.4.3. If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unless otherwise specified.

rules.title: You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit.
rules.text: 5.7.5. You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit. See CARD TYPES > Legends.

rules.title: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.
rules.text: 5.7.6. A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.

rules.title: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.
rules.text: 5.7.7. There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.

rules.title: Trash Area
rules.text: 5.9. ### Trash Area

rules.title: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).
rules.text: 5.9.1. The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).

rules.title: The trash is a public area.
rules.text: 5.9.2. The trash is a public area.

rules.title: Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these ca…
rules.text: 5.9.3. Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these cards.

rules.title: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.
rules.text: 5.9.4. When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

rules.title: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.
rules.text: 5.9.4.1. If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.

rules.title: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash.
rules.text: 5.9.4.2. Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash. The cards in the trash should always remain in the face-up position unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: A legal deck of Cyberpunk TCG cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.
rules.text: 7.3. A legal deck of *Cyberpunk TCG* cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.

rules.title: You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name.
rules.text:
7.3.1. You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name. See Name.

> **EXAMPLE:** The Legends “V: Corporate Exile” and “V: Streetkid” are both named “V,” so you can’t use both of them in the same deck.

rules.title: Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.
rules.text: 7.3.2. Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.

rules.title: Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (e…
rules.text: 7.3.3. Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (even if they have different card numbers).

rules.title: Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits.
rules.text: 7.3.4. Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits. See RAM & Color.

rules.title: If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.
rules.text: 7.3.5. If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.

rules.title: All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.
rules.text: 7.3.6. All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.

rules.title: Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.
rules.text: 7.3.7. Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.

rules.title: Randomize and place your Legends.
rules.text: 7.7. ### Randomize and place your Legends.

rules.title: Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.
rules.text: 7.7.1. Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.

rules.title: When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival.
rules.text: 7.7.2. When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival. Your Rival may “cut the deck” of Legends for you, if they choose.

rules.title: Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.
rules.text: 7.7.3. Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.

rules.title: The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends.
rules.text: 7.7.4. The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends. These two Legends don’t ready on the starting turn.

rules.title: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react.
rules.text: 9.7. During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react. They may take as many reactions as they want, in any order they choose.

rules.title: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.
rules.text: 9.7.1. You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.

rules.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.8. You may Call a Legend as a reaction. See Call a Legend.

rules.title: You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.9. You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.

rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.
rules.text: 9.9.1. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.

rules.title: You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.10. You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction. See TERMS > Effect Keywords > QUICK.

rules.title: If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.10.1. If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.

rules.title: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending.
rules.text: 9.11. If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before the defending player may take another reaction. See EFFECTS > Triggered Effects.

rules.title: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, th…
rules.text: 9.12. At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step.

rules.title: An effect is card text that affects the game.
rules.text: 10.1. An effect is card text that affects the game. Card text is the source of effects.

rules.title: Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.
rules.text: 10.1.1. Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.

rules.title: Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.
rules.text: 10.1.2. Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.

rules.title: When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers t…
rules.text: 10.1.3. When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers to the source of that effect unless another rule or effect says otherwise.

rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.
rules.text: 10.1.4. If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.

rules.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
rules.text: 10.2. To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

rules.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

rules.title: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed b…
rules.text: 10.2.2. If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival.

rules.title: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the…
rules.text: 10.2.3. Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving.

rules.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.
rules.text: 10.2.4. Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects. If an effect triggers in the middle of an activation or resolution, it becomes “pending resolution.” See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.title: An effect may include conditions.
rules.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.
rules.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.title: There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.
rules.text: 10.4. There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.

rules.title: A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.
rules.text: 10.4.1. A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.

rules.title: You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.
rules.text: 10.4.2. You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.

rules.title: A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.
rules.text: 10.4.3. A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.

rules.title: A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.
rules.text: 10.4.4. A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.

rules.title: An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.
rules.text: 10.5. An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.

rules.title: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.
rules.text: 10.6. An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

rules.title: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.
rules.text: 10.6.1. If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

rules.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
rules.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.title: If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does…
rules.text: 10.7. If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does not make a choice.

rules.title: If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, t…
rules.text: 10.8. If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, the effect is invalid and you cannot activate it.

rules.title: If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.
rules.text: 10.9. If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.

rules.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

rules.title: If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information fr…
rules.text: 10.10.1. If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information from when the piece was last valid.

rules.title: A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.
rules.text: 10.11. A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.

rules.title: You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.
rules.text: 10.11.1. You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.

rules.title: Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.
rules.text: 10.11.2. Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.

rules.title: After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.
rules.text: 10.11.3. After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.

rules.title: If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.
rules.text: 10.12. If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.

rules.title: If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before t…
rules.text: 10.13. If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs.

rules.title: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too.
rules.text: 10.14. If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too. Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects.

rules.title: If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending eff…
rules.text: 10.14.1. If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending effects finishes resolving all of their pending effects (including the new ones) before their Rival resolves their new ones.

rules.title: Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect…
rules.text: 10.15. Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution).

rules.title: If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when…
rules.text: 10.15.1. If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when the effect resolves.

rules.title: A triggered effect has a trigger condition.
rules.text: 10.16. A triggered effect has a trigger condition.

rules.title: A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.
rules.text: 10.16.1. A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.

rules.title: If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.
rules.text: 10.16.2. If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.

rules.title: If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that con…
rules.text:
10.16.3. If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that condition is met.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "When this Unit steals a Gig, increase it by up to 5.” In this example, the trigger is “When this Unit steals a Gig.” If the Unit steals 2 Gigs at the same time, then the effect “increase it by up to 5” becomes pending twice.

rules.title: Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when…
rules.text: 10.17. Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when,” “at the start of,” “at the end of,” and variations thereof. See TERMS > Trigger Keywords.

rules.title: You may activate “activated effects” as an action during your Main Phase.
rules.text: 10.18. You may activate “activated effects” as an action during your Main Phase. See Activate an Effect.

rules.title: You cannot activate an activated effect while resolving another action or effect, nor while any effects are pending r…
rules.text: 10.18.1. You cannot activate an activated effect while resolving another action or effect, nor while any effects are pending resolution.

rules.title: When an activated effect has a colon, the bolded text preceding the colon is the activation cost, and the text follow…
rules.text:
10.19. When an activated effect has a colon, the bolded text preceding the colon is the activation cost, and the text following the colon is the effect that resolves after you pay the activation cost. See Cost.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "[Spend Icon] Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.” This is an activated effect. During your Main Phase, you may spend the Unit as an activation cost; if you do, you gain the effect “Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.”

rules.title: Choices and costs before the colon are made or paid while activating the effect.
rules.text: 10.19.1. Choices and costs before the colon are made or paid while activating the effect. Choices after the colon are made while resolving the effect.

rules.title: You must pay all activation costs for an effect.
rules.text: 10.19.2. You must pay all activation costs for an effect. If you can’t pay all required costs, you cannot activate the effect.

rules.title: If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.
rules.text: 10.19.3. If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.

rules.title: Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.
rules.text: 10.20. Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.

rules.title: Choose a valid friendly effect to activate.
rules.text: 10.20.1. Choose a valid friendly effect to activate. See EFFECTS > Valid & Invalid Effects.

rules.title: If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.
rules.text: 10.20.2. If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.

rules.title: If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.
rules.text: 10.20.3. If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.

rules.title: Pay all activation costs in the order they appear.
rules.text: 10.20.4. Pay all activation costs in the order they appear. When you do, any effects triggered by the activation become pending.

rules.title: Communicate the effect and any choices/targets to your Rival.
rules.text: 10.20.5. Communicate the effect and any choices/targets to your Rival.

rules.title: Resolve the effect.
rules.text: 10.20.6. Resolve the effect. When you do, any effects triggered by the resolution become pending.

rules.title: Resolve any pending effects.
rules.text: 10.20.7. Resolve any pending effects.

rules.title: Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.
rules.text: 10.21. Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.

rules.title: A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.
rules.text: 10.22. A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.

rules.title: A persistent effect is not activated.
rules.text: 10.22.1. A persistent effect is not activated.

rules.title: A persistent effect never becomes pending.
rules.text: 10.22.2. A persistent effect never becomes pending.

rules.title: A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.
rules.text: 10.22.3. A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.

rules.title: If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.
rules.text:
10.23. If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit's effect text reads "Other friendly Units have +2 power while attacking.” The Unit only gains +2 from the moment the Unit attacks until the attack ends.

rules.title: When a persistent effect’s duration ends, that effect stops applying immediately once there are no other pending effe…
rules.text: 10.23.1. When a persistent effect’s duration ends, that effect stops applying immediately once there are no other pending effects.

rules.title: A replacement effect replaces one action or process with another.
rules.text:
10.24. A replacement effect replaces one action or process with another. (They often use “would” and “instead.”)

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit inherits the effect text from a Gear that reads "If this Unit would be defeated, defeat its "DEADMAN TRANSMITTER" instead.” The effect “defeat [this Unit’s] "DEADMAN TRANSMITTER"” replaces the game process of defeating the Unit.

rules.title: A replacement effect applies before (and instead of) the action or process it replaces.
rules.text: 10.25. A replacement effect applies before (and instead of) the action or process it replaces. The replaced action or process does not occur at all.

rules.title: If a replacement effect is optional, the player who controls that replacement effect may choose not to apply it.
rules.text: 10.26. If a replacement effect is optional, the player who controls that replacement effect may choose not to apply it.

rules.title: If it’s not possible to perform the replacement, that replacement effect cannot be applied.
rules.text: 10.27. If it’s not possible to perform the replacement, that replacement effect cannot be applied.

rules.title: If one or more replacement effects could apply to the same action or process, apply mandatory replacement effects bef…
rules.text: 10.28. If one or more replacement effects could apply to the same action or process, apply mandatory replacement effects before optional replacement effects.

rules.title: If multiple mandatory replacement effects could apply to the same action or process, the affected player (or the cont…
rules.text: 10.28.1. If multiple mandatory replacement effects could apply to the same action or process, the affected player (or the controller of the affected card) chooses which one to apply.

rules.title: If multiple optional replacement effects are chosen to apply to the same action or process, the affected player (or t…
rules.text: 10.28.2. If multiple optional replacement effects are chosen to apply to the same action or process, the affected player (or the controller of the affected card) chooses which one to apply.

rules.title: After a replacement effect is applied, check whether any other replacement effects can still apply to the new action…
rules.text: 10.29. After a replacement effect is applied, check whether any other replacement effects can still apply to the new action or process.

rules.title: Once a replacement effect has been applied to an action or process, that same replacement effect cannot apply to that…
rules.text: 10.29.1. Once a replacement effect has been applied to an action or process, that same replacement effect cannot apply to that same action or process again.

rules.title: A replacement effect from a game mechanic supersedes mandatory replacement effects.
rules.text: 10.30. A replacement effect from a game mechanic supersedes mandatory replacement effects.

rules.title: If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect in…
rules.text: 10.31. If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect instructs the player to make that choice.

rules.title: If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.
rules.text: 10.31.1. If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
rules.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.
rules.text: 10.31.3. If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.

rules.title: If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.
rules.text: 10.32. If multiple choices are required while resolving an effect, make those choices in the order written.

rules.title: If an effect instructs multiple players to make choices at the same time, the turn player makes their choices first,…
rules.text: 10.33. If an effect instructs multiple players to make choices at the same time, the turn player makes their choices first, followed by their Rival.

rules.title: [Star] Street Cred
rules.text: 11.2. ### [Star] Street Cred

rules.title: Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.
rules.text: 11.2.1. Your “Street Cred” is the sum of all Gig dice values in the friendly Gig area.

rules.title: The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.
rules.text: 11.2.2. The [Star] symbol is shorthand for Street Cred.

rules.title: When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred.
rules.text: 11.2.3. When you have no Gigs in your Gig area you have Null ( - ) Street Cred. Null does not count as having 0.

rules.title: Lag
Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.
rules.text: 11.3.1. Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
rules.text: 11.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack.

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
rules.text: 11.3.1.2. Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

rules.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
rules.text: 11.3.2. At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

rules.title: Equip
“Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it.
rules.text: 11.6.1. “Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it. When you do, the Gear becomes “equipped to” that card. See CARD TYPES > Gear.

rules.title: When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.
rules.text: 11.6.1.1. When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.

rules.title: Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area…
rules.text: 11.6.1.2. Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area or field.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”
rules.text: 11.6.2. A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”

rules.title: A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”
rules.text: 11.6.3. A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”

rules.title: Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.
rules.text: 11.6.4. Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.

rules.title: Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.
rules.text: 11.6.5. Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.

rules.title: "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another…
rules.text: 11.6.6. "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another valid Unit or Legend.

rules.title: Reveal
rules.text: 11.14. ### Reveal

rules.title: "Reveal" is a game action in which you show designated cards to your Rival.
rules.text: 11.14.1. "Reveal" is a game action in which you show designated cards to your Rival.

rules.title: Revealing a card is not removing it from the designated area unless specified after effect resolution.
rules.text: 11.14.2. Revealing a card is not removing it from the designated area unless specified after effect resolution. (Such as adding a revealed card to hand.)

rules.title: While revealing a card, make sure it is shown in a face up position, such that either player may read the card.
rules.text: 11.14.3. While revealing a card, make sure it is shown in a face up position, such that either player may read the card.

rules.title: Once a revealed card has been placed back face-down, it is hidden and can no longer be looked at unless otherwise spe…
rules.text: 11.14.4. Once a revealed card has been placed back face-down, it is hidden and can no longer be looked at unless otherwise specified.

rules.title: [ATTACK]
The [ATTACK] trigger is shorthand for “When this Unit attacks, [...]”
rules.text: 11.21.1. The [ATTACK] trigger is shorthand for “When this Unit attacks, [...]”

rules.title: The effect attached to the [ATTACK] trigger enters pending when you spend the Unit for the purpose of declaring an at…
rules.text: 11.21.2. The effect attached to the [ATTACK] trigger enters pending when you spend the Unit for the purpose of declaring an attack.

rules.title: Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s).
rules.text: 11.21.2.1. Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s). See EFFECTS.

rules.title: Resolve all pending [ATTACK] effects before your Rival’s react step.
rules.text: 11.21.2.2. Resolve all pending [ATTACK] effects before your Rival’s react step. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > React Step.

rules.title: Effect keywords are a shorthand for specific effects.
rules.text: 11.22. Effect keywords are a shorthand for specific effects.

rules.title: [BLOCKER]
The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to…
rules.text: 11.24.1. The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to it instead.“

rules.title: Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.
rules.text: 11.24.2. Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.

rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.
rules.text: 11.24.3. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.

decisions.shape: Yellow RAM2 cost1 printed power0 sellable Cyberware Gear. Default equip and inherited BLOCKER only; no trigger/static bonus/restriction omitted. Explicit zero printed-power inheritance retained.
decisions.inheritance: 3.18.3,4.11.3,4.11.3.1,11.6.4: bottom textbox read on current host while equipped; physical source Gear, subject host, controller host. Reminder text has no independent game effect (3.18.1.2.2.1).
decisions.lifetime: 4.10.2/4.12.1: derived only while legally equipped in field/Legends; departure immediately removes grant. Source history is not a pending triggered ability.
decisions.blocker: 9.9/11.24: ready Unit spends itself in rival React and becomes defending Unit. Same reducer for printed/inherited. 11.3 forbids Lag attacks/Spend-icon effects, not separately defined BLOCKER.
decisions.legend: 4.2.1 grants Unit type to field Legends, not Legends-area Legends. Legends-area host may inherit text but cannot declare Unit-only BLOCKER. No Go Solo/field-Legend admission.
decisions.duplicates: No blanket duplicate-keyword rule found in pinned capture. Retain each inherited text/source, project one existential BLOCKER permission and equivalent host spend/redirect action under9.9/11.24; paying once spends host so second source does not allow a second immediate declaration. No general stacking claim.
decisions.future: Kiroshi equip erratum already reflected in raw text; private friendly Legend look requires separate reviewed visibility/lifetime. Dying Night requires inherited ATTACK decrease and named-V end-turn ready2Eddies. Both remain unadmitted.
